sections.h2: Where is Suffolk, Virginia, and why is the city so large?
sections.html:
Suffolk is an independent city in the Hampton Roads region of southeastern Virginia, and it is the largest city in the state by land area. It covers 428.91 square miles, with 399.17 of them land and 29.74 water, at an elevation of 39 feet.

The size comes from a merger. In 1974 the city of Suffolk joined the independent city of Nansemond, the former Nansemond County, and the towns of Holland and Whaleyville, all under Suffolk's name and charter. Part of the Great Dismal Swamp lies inside the city, and the Nansemond and James rivers give it miles of waterfront.

The 2020 census counted 94,324 people, and the 2025 Census Bureau estimate is 104,699. Because the city spans farmland, swamp, small villages and a suburban north end, a house in one part of Suffolk can differ sharply from one in another.

Suffolk is divided politically into seven boroughs: Chuckatuck, Cypress, Holy Neck, Nansemond, Sleepy Hole, Suffolk and Whaleyville. The Suffolk borough matches the former city, and the other six match the six magisterial districts of the old Nansemond County.

  • Whaleyville, Holy Neck and Chuckatuck are the more rural boroughs.
  • Nansemond, Suffolk, Sleepy Hole and Cypress are the more urban ones.
  • The city plans a bypass around the crossroads community of Whaleyville in the southwest under its comprehensive plan.
  • The Driver Historic District and the Suffolk Historic District are among the city's listed attractions.

When you describe your property to a buyer, name the borough. It tells them what kind of lot, road and surroundings to expect.

Colonists founded Suffolk in 1742 as a port town on the Nansemond River, first called Constant's Warehouse. It was renamed for Suffolk in England, became an incorporated town in 1808, and became a city in 1910.

Railroads and later highways made it a transportation gateway east into South Hampton Roads. Peanuts then became the signature crop, and Planters' Peanuts was established here beginning in 1912. The company's founder Amedeo Obici and the Mr. Peanut mascot are part of local history, and the city has held its Peanut Fest every fall since 1977.

Suffolk is a peanut processing center, a rail and highway hub, and a home to defense contractors and distribution centers. The mix gives the city jobs in farming, logistics, manufacturing and technology.

SectorEmployers named on Wikipedia
Food and beveragePlanters Peanuts, Unilever, Lipton Tea, Massimo Zanetti Beverage Group

The U.S. Joint Forces Command, which stood near U.S. 17 and Interstate 664, was disestablished in August 2011. Joint training functions stayed in the buildings, and Navy cyber commands were expected to fill space there in 2013, adding about 1,000 jobs. City officials called the move a boon to north Suffolk.

sections.h2: Which roads and rail lines serve Suffolk?
sections.html:
U.S. 13, 17, 58, 258 and 460 and State Route 10 serve Suffolk, and Interstate 664 crosses the northeastern edge as part of the Hampton Roads Beltway. The Monitor-Merrimac Memorial Bridge-Tunnel links the city to Newport News.

  • Suffolk took over its own road system from the Virginia Department of Transportation on July 1, 2006.
  • Suffolk Transit runs local buses, with two connections to Hampton Roads Transit.
  • Three freight railroads serve the city.
  • A branch of a proposed Southeast High Speed Rail corridor between Petersburg and South Hampton Roads has been studied.

Because Suffolk has run its own road system since 2006, ask the city about any road or ditch question near your house.

sections.h2: What does Suffolk's climate mean for a house?
sections.html:
Suffolk has a humid subtropical climate with hot, humid summers and mild to cool winters. Annual precipitation averages 51.82 inches, and snow adds about 5.8 inches a year.

MeasureSuffolk, 1991 to 2020 normals
Mean daily high in July86.8 F
Mean daily low in January31.1 F
Average yearly precipitation51.82 inches
Wet days per year123.7
Record high105 F

With wet weather on about a third of days and a swamp-edged landscape, inspectors look at gutters, crawl spaces, drainage and air conditioning. Cleaning and servicing those before you sell can shorten the repair request list.

sections.h2: What do Suffolk's housing figures look like?
sections.html:
The 2020 census recorded 38,364 housing units in Suffolk, and 7.3 percent were vacant. There were 35,555 households, and half of them were married couples.

The homeowner vacancy rate was 2.2 percent and the rental vacancy rate was 8.2 percent. About 27.1 percent of residents lived in rural areas, and the city runs a land use program for farm and forest land.

sections.h2: What is the Suffolk real estate tax rate?
sections.html:
Suffolk charges $1.06 per $100 of assessed value citywide, with higher rates in two special districts. The Treasurer's page lists the rates as effective through June 30, 2027.

AreaRate per $100 of assessed value
Citywide$1.06
Downtown Business District$1.165
Route 17 Taxing District$1.30

Real estate tax is due in two installments, December 5 and June 5, or the next business day if either lands on a weekend or holiday. On a $300,000 assessment the citywide rate gives $3,180 a year, split into two $1,590 bills. Check whether your address lies in a special district before you estimate your bill.

Two Treasurer offices serve the public. The downtown office is at 442 West Washington Street, and the North Suffolk office is at 2000 Bennetts Creek Park Road. Both are open Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m., and the phone number is 757-514-4275.

sections.h2: How do Suffolk's assessor, tax relief and abatement programs work?
sections.html:
The City Assessor's Office, at 442 W. Washington Street, lists and values all real property, and the phone number is 757-514-7475. Proposed assessment property record cards are available only to the property's owner of record.

  • Tax relief for seniors, disabled veterans and disabled citizens is overseen by Social Services.
  • A rehabilitation abatement gives a partial exemption for qualifying renovation or replacement of structures in maturing neighborhoods.
  • A land use program values agricultural, horticultural and forest land by use instead of market value.
  • The assessor's office earned an IAAO Certificate of Excellence in Assessment Administration in 2025.

If you disagree with a value, state law lets you bring the complaint to the Board of Equalization, where the owner has to rebut the presumption that the assessor is right. The Assessment Process page on the city site explains your rights and deadlines, so read it before you file.

sections.h2: What happens to Suffolk property tax at a sale?
sections.html:
Suffolk's tax lien is paid out of the sale price, ahead of other liens, and the Treasurer releases it once the tax is paid. The buyer or trustee must send proceeds to taxes, including penalties and interest.

  • The seller pays Virginia's grantor tax of 50 cents per $500 unless the contract says otherwise.
  • Property taxes for the current year are prorated by contract.
  • Delinquent land can be sold by court after a set period, and the city must give notice 30 days before suing.
  • The treasurer can agree to a payment plan of up to 72 months.

We could not confirm Suffolk's late penalty or interest rate from an opened page, so ask the Treasurer for a payoff on your closing date.

faqs.q: What is Suffolk's real estate tax rate?
faqs.a: The Treasurer's page lists $1.06 per $100 citywide, $1.165 in the Downtown Business District and $1.30 in the Route 17 Taxing District. Those rates are listed as effective through June 30, 2027.

faqs.q: When is Suffolk property tax due?
faqs.a: Real estate tax is due December 5 for the first half and June 5 for the second half, or the next business day. Weekends and holidays move processing to the next business day.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Suffolk assessment?
faqs.a: Call the City Assessor's Office at 757-514-7475. Its office is at 442 W. Washington Street. Proposed assessment record cards are only released to the owner of record.

faqs.q: Is Suffolk the largest city in Virginia?
faqs.a: By land area, yes. Suffolk has about 399 square miles of land, which is the most of any Virginia city. By population it is far smaller, with 94,324 residents in 2020.

faqs.q: Does Suffolk have a program for farm or forest land?
faqs.a: Yes. The city's land use program bases tax on use value instead of market value for agricultural, horticultural and forest uses. Owners must meet the program's requirements, so ask the assessor.
